text.text:
Great location and beautiful hotel. Walking distance from public transportation and the ferry building.
If you are staying in a room on the same side of the restaurant be warned that you will hear the noise mornings and evenings from the people downstairs.  Rooms further away might be a better choice next time.  Breakfast buffet was too expensive imo.  You can walk over to the ferry building and enjoy something from the shops there instead.

text.text: Ive always came here with my boyfriend whenever we’re in SF together, it’s always has such a great atmosphere and it’s always the best. The amenities, the room, the service is spot on, even the people that come here to book-in. I’ve seen people come here from their weddings, graduations, traveling, business trips. It’s a nice experience if you plan on being in the Embarcadero area or close to the piers. The rooms were always clean, the people working are helpful and kind. I didn’t know that there was an ice machine, I thought that was interesting. Also the gym they have here made me think it’s pretty neat to have this at a hotel. I think one thing that I wish could change is the food delivery service, since you would have to pick up your food from downstairs instead of them bringing it up to your room. That might just be me but 🤷

text.text:
Truly a different type of hotel stay. Service was absolutely exceptional and attention to detail was meticulous. Impossible to enter or exit without having the front door held. Greeted with a smile every time I entered the lobby. Restaurant service was prompt & professional.

Amenities are great - we made frequent use of the available e-bikes as well as the free hotel shuttle service. I was also continually impressed by the hotel’s thoughtful, artful, and even outright playful design touches. Hidden reading lamps tucked into the headboard, hourglass timer in the shower discouraging water waste, recyclable wooden room keys, and even beekeeping on the property’s roof. Most of the time when a business touts sustainability it feels gimmicky - not at 1 Hotel.

Finally, truly could not ask for a better location. Walking distance to MoMa, Pier39, and great restaurants. Will definitely be back soon.

text.text:
Early Jan2025  Spent the tail-end of our long vacation with a stay at this hotel that used to be Hotel Vitale.

We had first heard about this chain which has a sister hotel in Toronto which we had visited a month before while travelling in Canada.

With eco-sustainability in mind, 1 Hotel has the best intentions but needs a lot of improvements in terms of execution.

Most of the eco styling is done in the look and feel with a lot of "green" touches in the decorative touches of the interiors while no particular innovative aspects were directly impacting the design of the rooms or its components.

The reusable water fountains in each floor is a good idea but the mechanisms are clunky and the glass vases are not sanitary due to the lack of a proper seal or cover.

These well intended ideas needed a more thoughtful deliberation to make sure that the quality and standards of the stay are not compromised.

Another issue we encountered was our main lamp which had a design flaw in the weight and wiring and had to be replaced on our first night in.

Other fixtures like light switches and outlets seem to be poorly positioned as well making them difficult to use.

Sherts and toiletries though were of good quality.

Service staff were helpful and quite friendly.

All in all, the ideal of the hotel is great but not sure whether the idea of luxury is consistently aligned with the execution of the operations.

We'd also recommend checking out the amenity benefits which are included in your stay.  One we got to try was the free 2 mi car service which could also be better in terms of distance allowance or other flexible options.

editorialSummary.text: Elegant quarters, some with bay views, in an upmarket hotel featuring a fitness center & Wi-Fi.

text.text:
We had a fantastic stay at the Four Seasons Embarcadero in October 2024. My husband and I were in SF to get married at City Hall, and although we hadn’t told the them the reason for our visit prior to check in, they asked when we arrived and immediately went above and beyond to make our stay incredibly special. We were joined by some good friends who also stayed at the hotel.

The rooms at the property are large, clean, and well appointed, with fantastic views of the city (we could see the Golden Gate Bridge as we had coffee each morning). The bathrooms were very nice, with separate tubs and standing showers. We used AMEX to book our stay, so had breakfast downstairs each morning, which was delicious and the servers were really friendly. If you want to save a little money on coffee, grab some when you walk in using the self serve stations. The property has a complimentary shuttle to locations nearby, which we used to get to dinner on a few occasions when it was raining.

One of the big surprises we came back to was a congratulations sign with champagne and balloons in our room. It was a simple gesture, but something we will never forget. We also spoke to several members of the team as we left for City Hall who told us their own wedding stories, which we really enjoyed and treasured. Another example of the team going above and beyond was one of the doormen letting us keep a rental car parked out front while we finished breakfast - extremely generous and unexpected (we were going to take turns circling the block while we each finished).

It truly was a trip we won’t forget and that was in large part due to our experience at the Four Seasons Embarcadero.

text.text:
I have been many times and it is always truly a five-star experience from start to finish. The property itself is stunning, featuring beautiful architecture and luxurious amenities that make you feel pampered at every turn.

The food at the hotel is exceptional, and the room service was perfect—prompt, delicious, and delivered with a smile. I especially appreciated how the staff went out of their way to ensure that every meal was a delightful experience.

What truly sets this hotel apart is the incredible team at the front desk and valet/ guest services who consistently demonstrate a commitment to excellence. From the moment I arrived, I was greeted with warmth and professionalism. The front desk staff were not only friendly but also genuinely helpful. They are truly amazing!

I was particularly touched by how the hotel celebrates special moments with guests. They went above and beyond to acknowledge my birthday and anniversaries, which made me feel truly valued and appreciated. Their attention to detail and thoughtful gestures show just how much they care about their guests.

In summary, while the Four Seasons boasts beautiful surroundings and excellent amenities, it is the outstanding personnel that elevate this hotel to a five-star experience. I cannot recommend this hotel highly enough.

We were locked out of our room for an hour because the batteries in the card key lock failed. Not to get into details, but many people knew that we were waiting to get back into our room, and told us that they would let us know promptly when the status had changed. However,  no one notified us of any updates about the status, until an hour later we went to the front desk where they told us that the lock had been fixed much earlier but they had "accidentally" not notified us . So after an exhausting day of business in SF, we were left hanging, waiting for re-entry when we could have been in our room much earlier. And this is after paying $700.00 a night for the privilege!  We told staff what we thought would be proper compensation for our inconvenience and they rejected our suggestion. Later, they did offer further compensation, but we resented having to haggle with the hotel about what we deserved as recompense for their error. We felt that they showed disrespect to us as repeat customers of the Four Seasons. And, the main job of a hotel is to provide a room, and on that account they failed. However, shout out to Robert, the Bellman, who was lovely, and helpful in every way.

text.text:
This is an excellent coworking space for engineers. Below are things I like about it:
- No music in the common area. This place is all about heads down focus work. I had to leave wework because they play music in every single common area I've been to (and I visited multiple offices in NYC and sf).
- Keurig coffee machine that has both decaf and caffeinated pods. I like this much more than wework, which provides "fresh brewed" coffee but only has it 9-5pm and only caffeinated, which is a huge problem if you work late and need a coffee to stay up.
- 24/7 access via app controlled lock. Wework gives you this but only if you get a dedicated desk. This is provided to all members, including ones who go for the cheaper hot desk option.
- Snacks provided completely for free (see pics) plus cereal and milk.
- Vending machines with wider selection. The killer for me is caffeine free Diet Coke, which it has. Also has ramen.
- Great common rooms that are generally free where you can have larger meetings.
- Access to a gym and roof terrace. Awesome for bringing friends over or having parties. This access is 24/7-- you just borrow the key fob, which is hung on the bulletin board in the office.
- They have events like bagel Friday's. Love these things.
- The place is windowless, but the design makes it seem like there are tinted windows (see pics). This is a polarizing feature, but I personally love the lack of real windows because I work late and get depressed when the sun starts to rise and I have to go home. Like I said-- this place is all about focus.
- All the chairs are soft and you can sit in them all day. Not like wework, which has hard chairs in the common areas and meeting rooms that hurt your butt after a while (possibly by design).
- They gave me a week to week membership for the common area for $90/week, which is a great deal in my opinion.

The story behind this place is it's in the basement of a hotel, and they used to use the space for storage. After doing this for a while, someone figured out they could redesign it as an office space and make more money. So they did, and that's what it is now.

I think if you're an engineer you'll love this place-- but as a creative type I think you'll hate it. Wework is probably a better option for creative types in my opinion.

I recently had a tech issue that was causing me a real headache and I'm so glad I found SF Connections. Not only did they provide me with a fantastic workspace, but the staff couldn't do enough to help. In particular, Aliea was an absolute superstar in solving my problem and really went above and beyond to make sure everything was up and running smoothly.

The workspace itself is excellent. It's clean, well-lit, and spacious, with plenty of room to work in peace and quiet. I really appreciated the snacks and beverages they provide on site, and the fact that they periodically have lunch on Fridays was a real treat. But it's really the staff who make the difference. They're all so friendly and helpful, and really go out of their way to make sure you're comfortable and have everything you need. Overall, I can't recommend SF Connections highly enough. Whether you need a workspace for a day, a week, or longer, this is the place to come!
